about: Per-line discounts, granted by the sales manager at approval. Every case here is a rule BOTH apps implement the same way. Open questions live in ../DIVERGENCES.md and must not be added until decided. Changing a case here is changing the rule, and needs both apps updated in the same pull request.

apply.why: ten per cent comes off the quoted rate and the amount is rebuilt from it

a second discount comes off the ORIGINAL rate, never the already discounted one - otherwise ten per cent given twice quietly becomes nineteen, and the quoted rate is gone for good after the first save
raising a discount reprices off the original rate, not the discounted one
removing a discount puts the original rate back
an order taken before discounts existed has price_list_rate 0 and must read as full price, never as free
a rate that will not divide evenly is still held to paise, so the lines add up to the total shown beneath them

totals.why: the two totals and the discount between them must reconcile by eye: before minus given equals after
the order-level percentage is given/before, NOT the mean of the line percentages - ten per cent off a small line and nothing off a large one is not a five per cent order
an order with nothing off reports no discount rather than a zero one
an empty order is zero, not an error

locked.why: an approved customer order is final
an approved LEAD order is final too - it has no custom_po_status, so asking only that field reads every lead order as still open, on exactly the orders that go on to become real ones
a locked rate counts as signed off whatever the status says
a pending order is still open

nobody moves a signed price, the general manager included - the GM override that exists for RATES does not extend to discounts. A rule that lets a signed price move from a desk but not from a counter is worse than either rule on its own. Settled 13 Aug 2026 in favour of the phone.

ceiling.about: Settled 13 Aug 2026: the phone's answer was taken whole. The dashboard used to clamp an out-of-range figure to the ceiling on the grounds that 150 meant 'as much as possible'. The likelier cause of 150 in a percentage box is a slip, and clamping turns that slip into a giveaway silently - which is the outcome a limit exists to prevent.

cases.why: nothing off is not a refusal
a fraction of a per cent is a real concession and must be accepted
a hair over the ceiling is refused, not rounded down to it
more than everything is refused on its own terms, before the ceiling is even reached for

expect.message: A discount cannot be more than 100%.

cases.why: a negative discount is a price rise wearing the wrong name

lead_fields.about: Lead Order Item is a custom child table with no standard pricing fields, so the same two numbers are spelled differently. One module on each side knows this and nothing else does.

cases.why: a lead order is written with the custom spelling and never the standard one
a customer order is written with the standard spelling, and carries discount_amount so ERPNext's own recalculation lands on the same net rate
reading is symmetrical: either spelling is understood wherever it is found
